notes: The extracted base bundle contains PB/Map/Config/YooAsset class definitions as MonoScript entries.

No live MonoBehaviour instances for PBGameLevelConfig, PBGameLevelData, PBGameMapConfig, MapConfig, LevelConfig, PBGameLevelBuilder, or YooAssetSettings were found in the base data.unity3d scene objects.
All 23 direct unity3d URLs copied from game.js preloadDataList returned 404 when probed against the public DATA_CDN root.
Likely second-stage GFCode/WebGL asset roots exist, because CommonFontAB/hwfont.ttf.unity3d is publicly reachable.
The exact bundle path or manifest path for gameplay/config assets is still not exposed by the local package.

observations: The remotecfg service is alive. GET returns 405 and OPTIONS/POST confirm the endpoints exist.
POST {} to /obtain and /obtain/param returns the same 80-byte base64 blob.
/obtain/param explicitly reports a missing JSON ObtainReq body when called without a body.
decodeV2 explicitly reports a missing EncodeDataDTO body when called without a body.
decodeV2 accepts JSON with an encodeData field, but the remotecfg blob still decodes only to opaque binary-like output rather than readable JSON/text.
encryptData requires login, so anonymous probing cannot produce a trusted local encode/decode round-trip.

blocker: The public data package is reachable and decodable, and the supporting remotecfg/decode backends are alive, but the actual level/map payload is not stored as plain TextAssets in the base bundle. The remaining payload is still hidden behind a second-stage GFCode/WebGL asset-bundle manifest, a protobuf/table asset layer, or a remote-config decode/parsing step that is not directly discoverable from the local package shell.
nextStep: Either capture the real second-stage bundle/manifest requests at runtime, or decompile the GFRunning/Assembly-CSharp asset-loading path deeply enough to recover the exact YooAsset/package URL builder plus the request/parse logic that turns the remotecfg blob into gameplay asset addresses.
